## Learning objectives

By the end of this demonstration, you should be able to explain what the
project's R lockfile records, how a Docker image becomes your MyBinder
session, and why we keep a record of the environment used to run an analysis.

## Why this matters

The same script can behave differently when package versions or system libraries change. We need to describe the environment alongside the code and the data version.

| Layer | What we record | Tool or file |
| --- | --- | --- |
| R runtime | R version | `renv.lock`, runtime information, container base image |
| R packages | Package versions and sources | renv and `renv.lock` |
| Wider environment | Operating-system libraries and rendering tools | Dockerfile and image |
| Code and configuration | The revision used for the run | Git commit |
| Actual session | Versions loaded when the analysis ran | `sessionInfo()` |

renv restores the R packages described by a lockfile. A Docker image can also
include the R interpreter, operating-system libraries, and rendering tools.
Binder starts a container from such an image in a browser. 

## Inspect the R environment

We can next view the contents of the renv.lock file:

```{r renv-contents, include = TRUE, echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE, cache = FALSE, output = TRUE, eval = FALSE}
file.edit("renv.lock")
```

The version of R running with your environment should ideally match the lock file.

```{r health-environments-session, include = TRUE, echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE, cache = FALSE, output = TRUE, eval = TRUE}
source("pipelines/workshop_support.R")
use_workshop_book_outputs()

R.version.string
packageVersion("renv")
```

Compare the running version with the reference version, **4.4.1**. A lockfile
records a version; it does not switch your running R session.

```{r health-environments-lockfile, include = TRUE, echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE, cache = FALSE, output = TRUE, eval = TRUE}
lock <- renv::lockfile_read("renv.lock")
lock$R$Version
workshop_packages <- c(
  "dataspice", "meta", "pins", "rfair", "rmarkdown",
  "synthpop", "targets", "vetiver"
)
vapply(
  workshop_packages,
  function(package) {
    record <- lock$Packages[[package]]
    if (is.null(record)) NA_character_ else record$Version
  },
  character(1)
)
renv::status()
```

The lockfile records exact package versions for the workshop. `renv::status()` checks whether the active library matches the lockfile.

The usual collaboration cycle is:

1. A maintainer prepares and tests the required packages.
2. The maintainer uses `renv::snapshot()` and reviews the resulting lockfile.
3. Collaborators use `renv::restore()` to obtain the recorded packages.
4. The analysis is tested in the restored environment.

The workshop's Binder image was built by restoring this lockfile, so you do not
need to run `renv::restore()` during the session.

## From a Dockerfile to RStudio on MyBinder {#environments-docker}

### Read the Dockerfile

A **Dockerfile** is a set of instructions for building a Docker image. Find
these instructions in the workshop's [Binder image Dockerfile](https://github.com/JBris/open-and-reproducible-science-in-r/blob/main/dockerfiles/binder/Dockerfile.1.0.0).

| Instruction | What it does in this project |
| --- | --- |
| `FROM rocker/binder:4.4.1 AS base` | Starts from Rocker’s Binder image for R 4.4.1. |
| `RUN` | Executes build steps such as installing system libraries and restoring R packages from `renv.lock`. |
| `COPY` | Adds files such as the lockfile and workshop lessons to the image. |

A **Docker build** uses these instructions and the repository files to produce
an **image**. A **container** is a running instance of an image. Each
participant runs the workshop in their own container started from the same
image.

### Launch the published environment

MyBinder prepares the launch image and starts a container on its servers. Because everyone starts from the same image, everyone has the same R version,
packages, and tools for the hands-on activities.

## Record the session

View and record the details of the current R session.

```{r health-environments-reload, include = TRUE, echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE, cache = FALSE, output = TRUE, eval = TRUE}
raw_file <- file.path("data", "raw", "healthwellbeing.rda")
stopifnot(
  file.exists(raw_file),
  identical(
    unname(tools::md5sum(raw_file)),
    "0d74964b0b7168379a2b015cb648b326"
  )
)
data_env <- new.env(parent = baseenv())
loaded_names <- load(raw_file, envir = data_env)
stopifnot(identical(loaded_names, "HealthWellbeing"))
health <- data_env[["HealthWellbeing"]]
stopifnot(nrow(health) == 29L, ncol(health) == 5L)

source("pipelines/workshop_support.R")
output_dir <- workshop_output_dir()
dir.create(output_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
writeLines(
  capture.output(sessionInfo()),
  file.path(output_dir, "session-info.txt")
)
file.edit(file.path(output_dir, "session-info.txt"))
```
